summary:
The BOLD Infrastructure for Alzheimer’s Reauthorization Act of 2024, Public Law 118-142, reauthorizes Federal funding authority for the Public Health Service Act program promoting public health knowledge and awareness of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias.

Section 1 provides the short title and is codified as a note to 42 U.S.C. 201.

Section 2 amends section 398B(e) of the Public Health Service Act, 42 U.S.C. 280c-5(e), which contains the authorization of appropriations for the program for promotion of public health knowledge and awareness of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias. The amendment inserts an additional authorization of appropriations of “$33,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029” before the period at the end of subsection (e). The Act thereby extends the program’s appropriations authorization through fiscal year 2029 at that annual level.

The Act does not make a direct appropriation, does not establish a new mandatory spending authority, and does not otherwise amend the substantive program authorities in section 398B. It includes no express conditions precedent, exceptions, rescissions, offsets, or separate sunset provision beyond the fiscal-year limitation inherent in the authorization of appropriations. The Act contains no special effective-date provision and therefore took effect upon enactment on December 11, 2024.
